verdicts.reason: A: the blue panel runs to the top and left canvas edges, which reads as a crop. The round 'UP TO 40% OFF' badge is squashed into a flat ellipse, and the CTA sits in the top row above the headline, so the reading order runs backwards. There is a large dead gap between that row and the headline, the subcopy leaves 'midnight.' orphaned, and the sky and glasses have shrunk to scraps. Still, the headline clearly leads and the logo keeps its size relative to the headline. B: the Meridian logo is blown up to roughly headline size and competes with the message. It has the same squashed badge, and the CTA is again above the headline. The badge, CTA and glasses are jammed against the top edge, and the glasses are pulled out of the scene into the panel. It's more cramped at the top and the brand balance is off, so A is the less bad of the two.
